summary: AquaTwin is a dual-agent GeoRAG system designed for agricultural policy planning in Maharashtra. It utilizes Sentinel-2 satellite data and soil moisture indices to model the environmental and economic impact of shifting 15% of water-heavy sugarcane fields to drought-resistant sorghum. To prevent the numerical hallucinations common in language models, the architecture intelligently separates semantic text searches from mathematical aggregations. When officials query exact water conservation metrics or financial transition subsidies, the system executes direct SQL against a PostGIS spatial database. This approach guarantees factual accuracy, translating complex remote sensing analytics into reliable, actionable insights for state governance.
details:
AquaTwin is a spatial analytics and policy forecasting dashboard designed to address agricultural water scarcity in Maharashtra, India. It provides government officials with a reliable, hallucination-free AI assistant to model the environmental and economic impacts of shifting 15% of water-heavy sugarcane fields to drought-resistant sorghum. The system solves the primary flaw in modern AI tools like mathematical hallucination by routing numerical questions directly to a spatial database rather than relying on language models to guess policy figures.

How It Works

The core engine relies on a dual-agent routing architecture to process user queries.

  • Spatial Data Pipeline: We extract Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and SMAP soil moisture data to compute agricultural metrics for 305 talukas in Maharashtra.
  • Dynamic Intent Routing: When a policymaker asks a question, the system evaluates the prompt for specific aggregation triggers.
  • Semantic GeoRAG: If the query is about policy strategy or text narratives, the router directs it to a vector database to retrieve regional context via semantic search, and the AI synthesizes an answer based strictly on those paragraphs.
  • Text-to-SQL: If the query requires math or aggregations (like finding the highest subsidy cost), the router intercepts it, compiles it into a PostgreSQL query, and executes it directly on our PostGIS backend to guarantee factual numbers.

Benefits

  • Factual Accuracy: Completely bypasses standard LLM math limitations by executing raw SQL for numerical policy queries.
  • Water Conservation Forecasting: Accurately projects liters of water saved per season based on satellite-derived crop coverage.
  • Economic Parity: Calculates the exact INR transition subsidies required to ensure farmers do not lose profit when switching to drought-resistant crops.
  • Interactive Mapping: Automatically renders spatial map pins on the dashboard by querying polygon centroids directly from the database during the chat.

Intended Impact

AquaTwin bridges the gap between raw satellite data and actionable state policy. By specifically modeling a 15% crop shift in Maharashtra, it gives policymakers the exact financial and environmental metrics needed to execute climate-resilient agriculture schemes without risking farmer livelihoods or relying on estimated data.

Development Tools and Technology Stack

  • Frontend: Streamlit (Python) for the interactive chat and mapping dashboard.
  • Backend Database: Supabase hosted PostgreSQL with PostGIS for spatial queries and pgvector for semantic search.
  • Spatial Data Engineering: GeoPandas, GeoPy, and OpenStreetMap APIs for boundary mapping and spatial cross-referencing.
  • Machine Learning: XGBoost for classifying water-intensive crops based on Sentinel-2 zonal statistics.
  • Local AI Infrastructure: Ollama running Llama 3.2 (for SQL compilation and synthesis) and Hugging Face all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (for vector embeddings).

Creativity and Innovation

The main innovation of AquaTwin is treating the AI strictly as a reasoning and routing engine rather than a database. Large language models frequently hallucinate numbers, making them dangerous for financial and policy planning. AquaTwin solves this by strictly separating semantic search from mathematical operations.

Furthermore, significant human engineering was required to sanitize the spatial datasets. During ingestion, 22 taluka polygons were completely unnamed in the raw spatial files. To fix this, I built an automated spatial cross-referencing script using GeoPy to ping OpenStreetMap coordinates, retrieve the correct region names based on their latitude and longitude centroids, and cleanly repair the PostGIS database. I also designed a secure SQL wrapper function to strip trailing semicolons from AI-generated subqueries, preventing runtime syntax errors and ensuring the backend remained strictly read-only.

Design Considerations

  • Precision over Fluidity: Built strict guardrails into the database functions to ensure all AI-generated SQL remains structurally valid and completely isolated from write privileges.
  • Data Integrity: Implemented fallback logic so if a user asks about a region that lacks agricultural data, the system explicitly admits a lack of data rather than guessing.
  • Resource Efficiency: Executed data ingestion workflows systematically to manage cloud RAM limits, running one taluka at a time and utilizing memory array downcasting.

Use of Artificial Intelligence (AI)

AI tools were utilized across both the live application architecture and the development workflow:

  • Application Core: The live dashboard uses local LLMs (Llama 3.2 via Ollama) and sentence transformers for active query routing, SQL compilation, and text synthesis.
  • Code Assistance: Used Gemini during the hackathon to brainstorm routing architectures, debug PostGIS subquery syntax errors, and optimize Python data engineering scripts to run cleanly in limited environments.
  • Documentation: Utilized Gemini to refine presentation text, audit previous NASA Space Apps repositories for structural standards, and review our codebase formatting for readability.
